Cc: Elena Park <elena@fulcrumpay.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: [Urgent] Sudden spike in 503s and tokenization latency impacting checkout

David —

We started seeing a sharp increase in 503 responses and tokenization timeouts around 08:40 PST this morning. Error rate for our payment verification route (POST /verify) jumped to ~12% and p99 latency climbed from ~180ms to 1.6s. Our retry logic is amplifying backlog and we have a visible queue buildup in the service that calls your inference endpoint.

Attached is a short sample of request/response logs and a trace where the LLM call timed out (fulcrumpay_error_sample.log). We raised a PagerDuty and our SRE (Elena) is on the line. This is impacting live transactions; customers are reporting failed checkouts.

Can you confirm whether there were any deploys or config changes on your side in the last hour? Any immediate mitigation suggestions — fallbacks, model routing, or capacity we can route to? This is high priority for FulcrumPay.

— Jamal
FulcrumPay — Head of Integrations

On Mon, May 24, 2027 at 09:25 AM David Kim <david@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — forwarding FulcrumPay escalation. Short summary: production 503s + p99 spike starting ~08:40 PST...

Quick update from infra triage (initial):
- No deploys in the serving fleet in the window (control plane shows last change 05:03 UTC).
- Observed a sudden increase in concurrent KV cache misses for the model shard serving this customer; miss rate jumped ~7x at 08:39 PST.
- Concurrent batch sizes spiked on a subset of nodes which caused tokenization fallbacks and kernel re-selection thrashing => elevated latency and 503s under queue pressure.

Immediate mitigations applied (09:38–09:42):
- Pinning affected nodes to lower max-batch to force smaller batches (reduces kernel thrash).
- Enabled immediate prefix/KV cache warmups for FulcrumPay keyspace.
- Routed small percentage (~15%) of traffic to a stable model variant (quantized v2) as fallback.

Observed effect: error rate dropped from ~12% to ~4% in 7 minutes; p99 moved from 1.6s to ~480ms but still above SLA. We're continuing to scale the dedicated pool and monitoring queue depth.

Next steps (owner: me unless noted):
- Short term (now): increase dedicated slot capacity for the account by +20% (if required, we have reserved headroom).
- 30m: run a targeted cache rehydrate for full keyspace.
- 2–4h: if instability persists, plan controlled rollback to the previous stable kernel set for affected nodes.

I'll join the bridge in 5. Posting live telemetry link in thread.

— Karthik
Director, Serving Runtime

Hi Jamal / Elena —

Thanks again for flagging this and for sharing the logs. I’m sorry for the disruption — we know this is customer-facing and unacceptable. Our tech team has implemented several mitigations (smaller batching, KV warmups, and a small fallback routing to quantized v2) which have already reduced error volume by ~65%. Karthik will continue monitoring.

Customer-facing commitments:
- Initial mitigation applied and we will continue to monitor for 60 minutes.
- If errors are not below 1% and p99 < 300ms by 60m, we will escalate to a controlled rollback and provide an exact ETA for resolution.
- We will provide a post-incident report and actionable next-steps within 48 hours, including timeline, root cause and any crediting for impacted API units.

Can you confirm current traffic pattern (batch size/peak TPS) or share any spike timing details you see on your end? That will help us correlate.

Apologies again — we’ll keep this thread updated and I’ll be on the bridge.

Best,
Marissa

Subject: RE: SignalFire — FulcrumPay latency & 503 spike: customer escalation and leadership handoff

Jamal / Elena —

Final status update: incident resolved and stabilizing. Summary:
- Root cause: sudden KV cache miss storm on the shard serving FulcrumPay which caused batch-size thrashing and kernel re-selection under load; this produced elevated p99 and 503s.
- Mitigations applied: small-batch caps, targeted cache rehydrate, temporary routing to quantized model v2, and incremental capacity increase for the account.
- Result: error rate reduced to <0.5% and p99 back to ~220ms by 02:15 PST; no further customer-visible failures since 02:20 PST.

Next steps and commitments:
1) Postmortem: Engineering will publish a full RCA and timeline within 48 hours (link to postmortem will be shared).
2) Reliability improvements: we will add cache-miss detection alerts, automated temporary pinning of batch caps for affected keyspaces, and a non-disruptive rehearsal of fallback routing in our staging fleet.
3) Credits: Marissa will follow up with a commercial credit proposal for impacted API units.

Attachments: runbook-failover-checklist.pdf; p99_latency_chart.png (pre/post).
Related links: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-78921; https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/fulcrum-escalation-logs

We appreciate the quick collaboration from Jamal and Elena — your traces made triage much faster. If you see any residual anomalies overnight, please ping the PD and we’ll re-open the bridge immediately.

— David
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
